A FAIR COMPARISON

The baseline matters.

The seasonal baseline predicts the same hour’s pickups from seven days earlier. The gradient boosting model uses calendar patterns and historical counts available before each midnight forecast origin.

Model settings were selected on validation data. Test outcomes were used only to score predictions; the model stayed fixed throughout the test.

KNOW THE LIMITS

A short, honest backtest.

Only seven complete days remain in the held-out evaluation after conservative daylight-saving exclusions. Results cover the 20 busiest zones selected using training data.

This is evidence from one historical quarter, not a guarantee of future accuracy. Weather, holidays, events, and supply constraints are not explicitly modeled.

DEFINITIONS

What the numbers mean

Observed demand: accepted completed taxi pickups, not all ride requests or unmet demand.

Fare revenue: the metered fare field for financially eligible trips. It excludes add-on charges and does not measure profit.

Total charges: the reported amount charged, including applicable recorded extras. Cash tips are not included in TLC totals.

Average fare: fare revenue divided by financially eligible trips. It does not use all pickup rows as its denominator.

MAE: mean absolute pickup-count error per zone-hour. WAPE: total absolute error divided by total observed pickups.

DATA QUALITY

Rules you can inspect

Financial eligibility requires finite, nonnegative fare and total fields within documented thresholds and payment types 0, 1, or 2. Other accepted pickups remain in demand analysis.

Unknown pickup zones, invalid timestamps, implausible durations and distances are excluded. Zero-distance trips can remain. Missing passenger counts do not remove trips.

Zero-filled zone-hours assume a complete monthly source file; vendor reporting completeness cannot be independently established.

FORECAST DESIGN

Past information only

Training and validation split at February 24. The test boundary is March 14, but daylight-saving exclusions leave March 25–31 as the effective test dates. Each of seven midnight origins produces 24 hourly predictions for 20 zones.

Features include hour, weekday, lags of 24, 168 and 336 wall-clock hours, and a trailing historical mean. No lag for a predicted hour reaches into that day’s forecast horizon.

For the April 1 snapshot forecast, the model is refit using all eligible observations through March 31. That refit is separate from the fixed model used for test metrics.

PROJECT STATUS

What you can reproduce

The Python cleaning and forecasting workflow has run on all three official monthly files. This website reads prepared aggregates; it does not query PostgreSQL.

All 567,817 hourly rows, the reporting queries, and forecast scores were verified in embedded PostgreSQL. The native warehouse load still requires an authenticated connection. Power BI project source passes structural schema checks; Windows Desktop refresh and visual validation remain.
